metadata.title: TraceCase: An Agent That Finds Out Why
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: Course pitch film, not a channel reel: opens on the hesitant writer per show-tell; no verdict card; no Your Turn (the assignment asks for a pitch, not a viewer exercise). Narrated as myself with my own name on the outro, as the assignment requires.
metadata.audience: INFO 7375 instructor and TAs; backend engineering hiring managers
metadata.source_doc: PROJECT-BRIEF.md (2026-10-13); HolmesGPT and AIOpsLab public pages (read 2026-10-13)

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Ashwin. When a service breaks, a dashboard tells you that something is wrong. It doesn't tell you why. So I want to build an agent that finds out, shows its evidence, and lets a person decide what happens next.

show.event: backspaces 'is it down?' → 'why is it down?'

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the monitoring question and corrects it to the real one: why.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: It's called TraceCase, and it isn't built yet. It will read a small Spring Boot service's logs, traces, and deploy history, and propose one fix. A person must approve that fix before it runs.

shot.visual_intent: A server stack sits left with a terracotta warning light; three sources (log page, trace bars, deploy timeline) appear beside it; a magnifying glass passes over them; a proposal card slides right and stops at a closed barrier arm.
shot.motion_claim: A server stack sits left with a terracotta warning light; three sources (log page, trace bars, deploy timeline) appear beside it; a magnifying glass passes over them; a proposal card slides right and stops at a closed barrier arm.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: When it's done, it will be one public repo: the demo service, the agent, an approval screen, failures I can trigger on purpose, and an evaluation report.

shot.visual_intent: An open repo box; five objects rise out of it one by one: server, magnifier, approval page, a red switch, report bars.
shot.motion_claim: An open repo box; five objects rise out of it one by one: server, magnifier, approval page, a red switch, report bars.

beats.narration_text: My Cloud Pulse team project answered one question: is the service healthy? When the answer is no, an engineer still digs through logs by hand, under pressure, to find out why.

shot.visual_intent: A health light goes from grey to terracotta; log pages pile up beside it; a cursor digs through them; a large question mark appears.
shot.motion_claim: A health light goes from grey to terracotta; log pages pile up beside it; a cursor digs through them; a large question mark appears.

beats.narration_text: Holmes G P T, an open-source agent, already investigates incidents, and asks a person before any change. Microsoft's A I Ops Lab evaluates agents like this, on Kubernetes. Or you dig by hand.

shot.visual_intent: Three plinths in a row, each with one object: a magnifier with a small approve gate, a lab flask on a cluster, a dashboard page with a cursor.
shot.motion_claim: Three plinths in a row, each with one object: a magnifier with a small approve gate, a lab flask on a cluster, a dashboard page with a cursor.

beats.narration_text: TraceCase will be smaller, and easy to check. It will run on a laptop with no Kubernetes, come with its own service to break, and every claim must point to a real log line or trace.

shot.visual_intent: A fourth plinth: TraceCase. A claim card with a leader line pinned to one trace span; then a barrier arm that stays down when the card is swapped.

show.event: gate stays shut on a mismatch

shot.motion_claim: A fourth plinth: TraceCase. A claim card with a leader line pinned to one trace span; then a barrier arm that stays down when the card is swapped.

beats.narration_text: A hiring manager for a backend role. In the first minute, they'll start the demo, break it with one command, watch the agent investigate, and approve or reject its fix.

shot.visual_intent: A terminal block; a switch flips and the service light turns terracotta; step cards appear one by one; a pair of approve / reject pills, the cursor clicks approve.
shot.motion_claim: A terminal block; a switch flips and the service light turns terracotta; step cards appear one by one; a pair of approve / reject pills, the cursor clicks approve.

beats.narration_text: What will it show about me? First, a loop with a budget. Observe, pick a tool, record the evidence, update the guess. It stops on a supported cause, or at a limit. Never because the model says it's done.

shot.visual_intent: Four stations on a ring (observe, tool, record, update); a terracotta dot travels the ring; a budget meter beside it drains with each lap; three exit doors light up one at a time.
shot.motion_claim: Four stations on a ring (observe, tool, record, update); a terracotta dot travels the ring; a budget meter beside it drains with each lap; three exit doors light up one at a time.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Second, control. Each step must match a fixed format, a prompt contract that code checks. Tools come from an allow-list, never a shell. And a claim citing evidence that doesn't exist is rejected.

shot.visual_intent: A short menu card of three safe actions with a lock; a shell prompt block is crossed out; then two claim slips: one pinned to a real span gets a check, one pinned to nothing gets a cross.
shot.motion_claim: A short menu card of three safe actions with a lock; a shell prompt block is crossed out; then two claim slips: one pinned to a real span gets a check, one pinned to nothing gets a cross.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Third, a human gate. The approval records the exact action, its target, and its evidence. If any of those change, it stops counting.

shot.visual_intent: An approval card with three fields and a seal; the barrier lifts; then one field changes, the seal breaks and the barrier drops again.
shot.motion_claim: An approval card with three fields and a seal; the barrier lifts; then one field changes, the seal breaks and the barrier drops again.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Fourth, evaluation. About thirty failure scenarios, ten locked away before I tune anything, against a summarize-the-logs baseline. I'll count right answers, honest I-don't-knows, and unsupported claims. I have no numbers yet.

shot.visual_intent: Thirty small tiles drop into a grid; ten of them slide into a locked box; a big hero counter reads '? / 10' because nothing has been measured.
shot.motion_claim: Thirty small tiles drop into a grid; ten of them slide into a locked box; a big hero counter reads '? / 10' because nothing has been measured.

beats.narration_text: The demo will be realistic: a Spring Boot API and a worker, Postgres, and Redis as a cache and a queue, so there are real failures to find, like a stale cache. Open Telemetry traces will tie it together.

shot.visual_intent: API and worker stacks, a Postgres cylinder, a dark Redis block between them; a queue of small crates backs up into the Redis block; one trace line threads through every part.
shot.motion_claim: API and worker stacks, a Postgres cylinder, a dark Redis block between them; a queue of small crates backs up into the Redis block; one trace line threads through every part.

beats.narration_text: In scope: one demo service, and failures I design. That's also my honest limit: it won't prove anything about real production systems. And it never runs arbitrary commands.

shot.visual_intent: A fenced square holds the service; a terminal prompt outside the fence is crossed out.
shot.motion_claim: A fenced square holds the service; a terminal prompt outside the fence is crossed out.

beats.narration_text: The first piece: the demo with one failure I can trigger, and a trace that shows it. A saved trace and a dated log will prove it ran.

shot.visual_intent: A service with a switch; the switch flips and one span on a trace waterfall turns terracotta; a dated log page slides underneath.
shot.motion_claim: A service with a switch; the switch flips and one span on a trace waterfall turns terracotta; a dated log page slides underneath.

beats.narration_text: The biggest risk is approving one thing and running another. So I'll trigger it on purpose. Approve fix A, swap in fix B, and the system must refuse until a person looks again.

shot.visual_intent: Card A is approved (seal); a hand-off swaps it for card B; the barrier stays down and a cross lands on B.
shot.motion_claim: Card A is approved (seal); a hand-off swaps it for card B; the barrier stays down and a cross lands on B.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? Mostly to learn. The jobs I apply for ask for agents, observability, and evaluation, and my resume doesn't show them yet. I'm building on Spring Boot work from Cloud Pulse, and language-model services from my My Ed Master internship.

shot.visual_intent: Two shelves: 'new' holds ghosted outline blocks; 'built before' holds solid blocks that land one by one.
shot.motion_claim: Two shelves: 'new' holds ghosted outline blocks; 'built before' holds solid blocks that land one by one.
